inputs.text:
TASK: Produce a source-aligned low-frequency color and tone layer for the first manga page while preserving the supplied line art exactly.

PRIORITY ORDER: 1) immutable source linework, screentones, text, and geometry, 2) no new visual structure, 3) consistent colors for repeated visible regions on this page, 4) complete broad-region colorization. If instructions conflict, follow the higher priority.

SOURCE AUTHORITY: The first input image is the sole authority for canvas, crop, panel layout, whitespace, composition, perspective, anatomy, pose, faces, hairstyle shape, clothing structure, props, architecture, terrain, smoke, effects, every contour, every edge, every screentone dot, hatching pattern, and existing light-and-shadow boundary. Preserve all existing visual boundaries in the same position, size, and shape. Never add, remove, complete, repair, simplify, or redesign content.

LOW-FREQUENCY COLOR ROLE: Fill only regions that already exist in the source. Generate broad, stable color fields and restrained low-frequency tonal separation; do not regenerate high-frequency detail. Treat source grayscale as the authority for structure, texture, and relative luminance, not as a requirement for the final image to remain gray. Preserve dense screentones and distant small characters without reconstructing, enlarging, cleaning, or simplifying them. Keep every color boundary aligned to an existing source boundary.

NO-REFERENCE COLOR POLICY: No external character reference image, named character palette, or Qwen3-VL character analysis is available. Do not invent canonical identity colors. Choose conservative, natural anime colors from visible grayscale values and surrounding regions. Keep repeated appearances and adjacent parts of the same visible person internally consistent using only the source page. Do not transfer a color from one person to another. Apply outfit colors only to clothing regions already present in the source.

TEXT AND GRAPHICS LOCK: Speech bubbles, caption boxes, narration boxes, signs, labels, logos, and sound-effect regions are immutable source regions. Preserve exact boundaries, white backgrounds, glyphs, punctuation, spacing, orientation, and line breaks. Keep text and ink neutral black. Do not translate, rewrite, regenerate, restyle, move, distort, obscure, or color text.

OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: Return the same manga page with broad color and tone added, not a redraw or reconstruction. Preserve the source high-frequency structure for the separate lineart protection stage.
